data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin 'Silvesterus', which comes from 'silva' meaning 'forest'. The name is believed to have been given to honor the forest gods, Silvanus and Silvana. The name Sylvester carries the meaning “Forest guardian” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Sylvester usually hope their child will grow to embody forest guardian and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name representing protection, guardianship, and the natural world.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sylvester total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: שלבסטר
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שלבסטר הוא שם האם בעברית, המגיע מהמילה בלבבאטשה (שלב בל באטה), שפירושו 'מלך היער'. על היות מגאטיבי ארבית בלבאטה חעבית ודול היוו ארבית מברבר איאאי שלשור וירנ סביאטה. ושה ארבית בלבאטה חעבית היוו ארבית בלבאטה ויול היוו שלשור וסריבת ויול איאאי.

in_latin.name: Sylvester
in_latin.long_meaning: Sylvester est nomen, quod a silva ortum est. Silva, quae significat forestem, est locus ubi arbores et aliae plantae crescunt. Nomen Sylvester, a silva, significat rex silvae. Rex, qui significat regem, est nomen quod dicitur alicui, qui dominus est overo suo. Sylvester est nomen quod significat dominus forestis. In early Christian church, nomen Sylvester erat nomen, quod significabat sanctitatem et virtutem. Nomen Sylvester, in Latin, significat rex silvae, qui est nomen, quod dicitur alicui, qui sanctus et virtuosus est.

in_english.name: Sylvester
in_english.meaning: forest king, king of the forest, ruler of the woods
in_english.long_meaning: The name Sylvester is derived from the Latin word 'silva', meaning forest, and is associated with the concept of a ruler or king. In Christian tradition, the name Sylvester is often linked to Saint Sylvester, who is said to have been a pope during the 4th century. The name Sylvester is also associated with the idea of sanctity and virtue, as it is said to signify a person who is holy and virtuous. In modern times, the name Sylvester has become popular as a given name, particularly in Christian cultures. It is often associated with qualities such as leadership, wisdom, and spiritual guidance.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sylvester gained popularity in the Christian world due to a tradition that began in Rome. The legend tells of Pope Sylvester I (circa 314–335 AD), who is described as having cured Emperor Constantine the Great of leprosy. In gratitude, Constantine allowed Christianity to flourish in Rome and Sylvester was made pope. The name Sylvester came to symbolize the spiritual and cultural triumph of Christianity over the pagan Roman Empire.
data.spiritual_significance: Sylvester is believed to be a strong name for those who are seeking spiritual growth and renewal. The association with the forest gods Silvanus and Silvana suggests deep connection with nature and an appreciation for the sacred in all things. Additionally, the presence of this name in early Christian history serves as a reminder of the power and resilience of the faith in the face of challenges.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sylvester: Derived from the Latin word "silvester," meaning "of the forest," symbolizing the hermit Sylvester I, who revered the wilderness in devotion and solitude, embodying the virtue of spiritual detachment.

historical_references.reference: Pope Sylvester I was a prominent pope who reigned from 314 to 335 AD during the early Christian period. He is often credited with the conversion of the Roman emperor Constantine I to Christianity. According to legend, Constantine visited Sylvester in Rome during the Battle of Milvian Bridge in 312 AD and saw a vision of the cross, which inspired him to convert and adopt Christianity as the state religion of the Roman Empire. Sylvester's importance lies in his role in consolidating the power of the papacy and establishing its independence from the secular Roman government.
historical_references.context: Early Christian period, Consolidation of papal power and independence from secular Roman government

historical_references.reference: Another Saint Sylvester, also known as Silvester I or Silvester of Rome, was a bishop who lived during the 5th century AD. He is the patron saint of Rome and is believed to have been the bishop of Rome during the time of Pope Leo I. According to legend, Sylvester was born in Ravenna, Italy, and was sent to Rome as a bishop by Leo I to combat the Donatist heresy. Sylvester's importance lies in his role in defending Rome against Attila the Hun and his success in converting the city to Christianity.
historical_references.context: Defending Rome against Attila the Hun, Conversion of Rome to Christianity
